Compute an Average Membership Degree (AMD) curve

Source: R/compute_amd_curve.R
compute_amd_curve.Rd

For every candidate number of configurations, this function runs fuzzy c-means from several random initializations. Random starts are computational attempts to estimate the same solution, not data replicates. Consequently, the fit with the smallest fuzzy c-means objective among the converged starts supplies the membership matrix evaluated by amd_score() at each c.

Usage

compute_amd_curve(
  data,
  its,
  nin,
  nsp,
  seeds = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE,
  plot_curve = FALSE,
  open_device = TRUE,
  scale_data = FALSE,
  iter_max = 100,
  m = 2,
  preselect_top_sd = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Numeric matrix or data frame. Rows are observations and columns are variables. Rows with missing values are removed with a warning and recorded in the returned row map.

its

Positive integer number of random starts for every candidate c.

nin

Minimum candidate number of configurations. Must be at least 2.

nsp

Maximum candidate number of configurations.

seeds

Optional positive integer vector or matrix. Vectors retain the historical start-major order; unused trailing values are ignored. If NULL, seeds are sampled from the caller's active random-number generator and advance its state. A matrix must have one row per start and uniquely named columns for every evaluated c; this form preserves the seeds of common candidates when the upper search limit is extended.

verbose

Logical; print progress information when TRUE.

plot_curve

Logical; plot the primary AMD curve when TRUE.

open_device

Logical; when plot_curve = TRUE, open a new graphics device before plotting. The default is TRUE for compatibility with the public 0.1.0 function. It has no effect when plot_curve = FALSE.

scale_data

Logical; standardize variables before fitting.

iter_max

Positive integer maximum number of fuzzy c-means iterations.

m

Fuzziness parameter; must be greater than one.

preselect_top_sd

Optional positive integer. If supplied, retain only the variables with the largest standard deviations before optional scaling. Retained variables are ordered by decreasing standard deviation; their original indices and names are recorded in settings.

Value

An object of class "amd_curve". schema_version identifies the public object layout. The primary curve contains AMD values from the minimum-objective converged fit at each c. Components mean, max, and raw retain the historical restart summaries for diagnostics and compatibility. These historical summaries include all starts, including nonconverged starts, and are not the primary curve. selected_fits contains the exact fitted memberships that produced the primary curve. complete_rows and omitted_rows map the fitted observations back to the input rows. The settings component records the input and retained variables and the exact centering and scaling vectors used to construct the fitted data. manifest_id links the curve to its process-level reproducibility manifest. Additional public components are c_peak, its historical alias c_opt, peak_at_boundary, the per-start objectives, iterations and converged matrices, selected-start diagnostics, the seed matrix, coordinates (the selected membership matrix at c_peak), backend, and selection_rule. selected_fit is the element of selected_fits corresponding to c_peak.

Details

AMD itself is defined independently of fuzzy c-means. Fuzzy c-means is the membership-estimation backend used by this function.

The returned c_peak (and its compatibility alias c_opt) is only the numerical maximum of the evaluated curve. In particular, a maximum at the boundary of the examined range is flagged and must not by itself be treated as evidence for that number of groups. If several evaluated values are exactly tied for the maximum, the smallest c is returned.

Vector seeds, including seeds generated when seeds = NULL, preserve the historical start-major mapping and therefore depend on the number of evaluated candidates. Use a named seed matrix when comparing nested search ranges. Extra named columns are allowed and ignored when their c is not in the current range. Duplicate seeds within one candidate c reduce the number of unique random starts and generate a warning.

Every curve contains a manifest_id linking it to the process-level record returned by amd_reproducibility_manifest(). Retrieve the manifest immediately after each curve and save one copy of every distinct identifier. Curves sharing an identifier can share the saved copy.

References

Mendoza, M. and Araújo, M. B. (2022). Biogeography of bird and mammal trophic structures. Ecography, 2022(5), e06289. doi:10.1111/ecog.06289

Examples

set.seed(42)
X <- rbind(
  matrix(rnorm(40, mean = -2), ncol = 2),
  matrix(rnorm(40, mean = 2), ncol = 2)
)
curve <- compute_amd_curve(
  X, its = 2, nin = 2, nsp = 3, seeds = 1:4, verbose = FALSE
)
curve$curve
#>         2         3 
#> 0.4353950 0.5243304
